sections.overview: The White-throated Needletail is a large migratory swift of eastern Asia and Australia, known in French as the Martinet épineux.
sections.identification: It has long curved, pointed wings, grey-brown plumage with a green gloss, a white throat and undertail, and a short tail whose projecting shafts look needle-like.
sections.habitat: Outside the breeding season it spends nearly all its time in the air over a wide range of landscapes, from forests to open country and coastal areas.
sections.diet: It catches flying insects such as termites, ants, beetles and flies in the air, often feeding in rising currents around storm fronts or fires.
sections.behavior: It spends much of its life on the wing, landing mainly to breed and roost.
sections.reproduction: It breeds in northeast Asia during the northern summer and migrates south to Australia for the non-breeding season.
sections.ecology: It belongs to Hirundapus, alongside other needletails such as the larger Brown-backed Needletail H. giganteus; its white throat and undertail help distinguish it in flight.
sections.conservation: The species is a non-breeding visitor to Australia and has a documented threatened-species determination in parts of that country; this regional status is not a global assessment.
